channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Rehabilitation of Athletes With Hamstring Strain Injury: SONAFE-Brazil Clinical Practice Guideline.
item.description: The National Society of Sports Physical Therapy (SONAFE-Brazil) released a clinical practice guideline for hamstring strain injury rehabilitation, utilizing the GRADE approach to synthesize evidence from randomized clinical trials for clinicians and athletes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Photobiomodulation therapy has a negligible effect as an adjunct to motor control exercise in people with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=148) found that adding photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) to motor control exercise provided negligible additional improvements in pain intensity (MD -0.4 points, 95% CI -1.2 to 0.4) or disability (MD -0.7 points, 95% CI -2.4 to 0.9) compared with sham PBMT in adults with chronic non-specific low back pain over 12 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A Return to Performance Continuum for Football (Soccer) Players After ACL Reconstruction: Bridging Rehabilitation, Return to Play and Sustained Performance.
item.description: This perspective outlines a four-stage Return to Performance (RTPperf) continuum for football players post-ACL reconstruction, emphasizing restoration of movement quality, progressive sport-specific technical/tactical retraining, physical reconditioning, and maximal strength/neuromuscular performance to bridge rehabilitation, return to play, and sustained performance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
item.description: A case series of 100 patients after quadriceps tendon autograft ACL reconstruction found that 3-month isometric quadriceps LSI strongly predicted 2-year IKDC scores (β = 3.9; adjusted R² = 0.36; P < .03), and 9-month isokinetic quadriceps LSI strongly predicted both Lysholm and IKDC scores (β = 3.9-4.7; adjusted R² = 0.34-0.35; P ≤ .003).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Post burn Cubital Tunnel Syndrome Electrophysiological and Functional Responses to High intensity Laser Therapy versus Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=75) compared HILT+UNGE, ESWT+UNGE, and UNGE alone for post-burn cubital tunnel syndrome. Both HILT and ESWT improved nerve conduction and upper-limb function more than UNGE alone (all P < .001). HILT produced significantly greater improvements than ESWT across electrophysiological outcomes and DASH scores, with benefits maintained at 12-week follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical performance clustering as a marker of frailty, fall risk, and cognitive health in older adults
item.description: An unsupervised classification study of 368 older adults identified three physical performance clusters (High, Moderate, Low), which differed significantly across most physical performance measures, especially muscular power and joint moments. The Low Physical Performance group included more frail individuals and fallers, supporting the utility of this clustering for identifying at-risk subgroups.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Reframing hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a measurement instrument rather than a technique debate: a theoretical framework applying COSMIN to HODA-A.
item.description: This theoretical paper proposes a Hands-On Data Acquisition and Analysis (HODA-A) framework, applying COSMIN principles to conceptualize hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a clinician-reported outcome measurement process rather than isolated manual techniques.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of thoracic kinesiological taping on pulmonary functions, respiratory muscle strength, and functional independence in patients with hemiplegia: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=30) found that thoracic kinesiology taping combined with conventional rehabilitation significantly improved pulmonary function (FVC, FEV1, PEF) and maximal inspiratory pressure, as well as Functional Independence Measure scores, in individuals with chronic post-stroke hemiplegia.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of kinesio taping and myofascial release therapy in cervicogenic headache: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=81) found that both kinesio taping and myofascial release, combined with home exercise, effectively reduced pain and headache frequency in cervicogenic headache. MFR provided more sustained improvements in disability and physical quality of life.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Is Reduced Spinal Range of Motion a Prognostic Factor for Pain Intensity, Disability, and Global Recovery in People With Specific or Nonspecific Spinal Pain? A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of 37 studies found very low certainty evidence regarding whether reduced spinal range of motion is a prognostic factor for pain, disability, or recovery in spinal pain patients, with inconsistent results and all studies rated as high risk of bias.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of iTBS and rTMS Combined with Robotic Rehabilitation on Ambulation and Lower Extremity Motor Function in Chronic SCI Patients.
item.description: An RCT found that intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) combined with robotic rehabilitation improved ambulation and lower extremity motor function in chronic spinal cord injury patients compared to sham, with no significant differences between active protocols.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Shear wave elastography for assessing lower extremity muscle stiffness after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
item.description: A systematic review concluded that shear wave elastography can detect muscle-specific stiffness deficits after ACL reconstruction, including reduced vastus medialis and semitendinosus stiffness, which correlate with function beyond strength, but standardized protocols are required for clinical guidance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of physiotherapy in reducing pain in subjects with temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review with network meta-analysis
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 25 RCTs (n=1,540) found that manual therapy and therapeutic exercise were effective for reducing pain in temporomandibular disorders, with multimodal treatments being most effective. The combination of dry needling and manual therapy appeared to be the most effective approach.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Can Psychological Readiness Predict Successful Return to Sports After Patellar Stabilization Surgery in Adolescent Patients? A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 97 adolescent patients found that an ACL-RSI score ≥59.2 was associated with an increased likelihood of successful return to sport (OR, 3.56; 95% CI, 1.10-11.51; P = .033) after patellar stabilization surgery, independent of sex or injury characteristics.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of conservative interventions on pain and disability in degenerative cervical spine disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (2,378 participants) found conservative interventions were associated with significant reductions in pain (SMD = -0.67; 95% CI, -0.97 to -0.37; I² = 87.20%) and disability (SMD = -0.60; 95% CI, -0.97 to -0.24; I² = 91.56%) in degenerative cervical spine disease, with acupuncture and exercise-based interventions showing benefit, but manual therapy showing no significant pooled benefit. The certainty of evidence was low.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy reduces pain in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain: a multicentre randomised controlled trial
item.description: A multicenter randomized controlled trial found that a smartphone-based multidisciplinary intervention combining personalized exercise and cognitive-behavioral therapy significantly improved pain, function, quality of life, and psychological well-being in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain. This digital therapeutic offers a scalable and cost-efficient delivery of care aligned with clinical guidelines.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: From information to action; co-designing pain neuroscience education for adolescents with low back pain: Focus group insights.
item.description: This qualitative study used focus groups (n=15 adolescents with LBP) to co-design pain neuroscience education (PNE) material. Findings highlighted the need for relatable, practical, engaging, and easy-to-navigate back-specific information, leading to the development of the "Back To Move" prototype.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Adherence to home-based exercise therapy in adults with non-specific chronic low back pain: a cross-sectional study of 491 participants of the ComPaRE cLBP e-cohort (ADHERE II).
item.description: A cross-sectional study (n=491) found that adherence to home-based exercise therapy was 45% in adults with non-specific chronic low back pain. Higher physical activity before cLBP onset, lower cLBP intensity, and lower treatment burden were associated with higher adherence, but supervision did not significantly influence it.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Continuity of care interventions for people with stroke and their caregivers: a scoping review of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: This scoping review of 80 RCTs found that continuity of care interventions for stroke most often included only stroke survivors and focused on the transition from acute to home care, often neglecting family-centered approaches and other critical transitions in the care continuum.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: "It's not for me": community-based fall prevention exercise programs for those aging into disability.
item.description: A qualitative study (n=11) with older adults aging into disability found multidimensional barriers to community-based fall prevention exercise programs, including lack of awareness, interconnected accessibility issues, stigma, and program misalignment, suggesting the need for co-designed, inclusive, and identity-affirming programs.
item.author: PubMed
